title: Wave 13: Wales/Heptarchy, Shiji Hegemons, Stokvis SE Asia/India, Landnámabók, Samaritans/Kordofan & Chronologers

nodes.name: King Coel Hen ('Old King Cole') of the Hen Ogledd
nodes.role: Progenitor of Northern British Dynasties (Coeling)
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Root patriarch of the Coeling dynasties of Rheged, Elmet, Ebrauc, and Gododdin across Skene's Four Ancient Books of Wales.

nodes.name: King Urien Rheged & Owain mab Urien
nodes.role: British King of Rheged & Patron of Taliesin
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Foremost northern British king celebrated in Taliesin's awdlau and Skene's Book of Taliesin; led coalition at Lindisfarne.

nodes.name: Taliesin Ben Beirdd (Chief Bard of Rheged)
nodes.role: Chief Brythonic Court Poet & Chronicler of Urien Rheged
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Composed historical praise poems preserved in Peniarth MS 2 (The Book of Taliesin, Skene Vol. 1).

nodes.name: Aneirin & King Mynyddog Mwynfawr of Gododdin
nodes.role: Poet of Y Gododdin & Lord of Din Eidyn (Edinburgh)
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Commemorated the 300 Brythonic warriors of Catraeth in the Book of Aneirin (Skene Vol. 1).

nodes.name: King Rhydderch Hael of Alt Clut (Strathclyde)
nodes.role: Christian King of Strathclyde & Ally of Urien and Columba
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
W.F. Skene, Chronicles of the Picts and Scots
nodes.notes: Descendant of Dyfnwal Hen and contemporary of St. Kentigern (Mungo) and Urien Rheged.

nodes.name: Llywarch Hen (Cousin of Urien & Poet of Powys)
nodes.role: Coeling Prince of South Rheged & Elegist in Red Book of Hergest
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Meirchion Gul whose surviving englynion mourn his twenty-four sons on the Welsh border.

nodes.name: Kings Idwal Iwrch & Cynan Dindaethwy of Gwynedd
nodes.role: Kings of Gwynedd Bridging Cadwaladr to Merfyn Frych
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Successors of Cadwaladr Fendigaid whose daughter Esyllt transmitted Gwynedd's claim to Merfyn Frych and Rhodri Mawr.

nodes.name: Prince Cynan ap Iago & Gruffydd ap Cynan
nodes.role: Restorer-King of Gwynedd & Hiberno-Norse Prince
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Exiled to Dublin with Hiberno-Norse allies before reclaiming Gwynedd; subject of Wales's oldest royal biography.

nodes.name: King Owain Gwynedd (Owain ap Gruffydd)
nodes.role: First Styled Princeps Wallensium (Prince of the Welsh)
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Halted Henry II's campaigns in Berwyn and fostered Llywelyn the Great's ancestral Aberffraw house.

nodes.name: Rhys ap Gruffydd ('The Lord Rhys' of Deheubarth)
nodes.role: Ruler of Deheubarth & Patron of First Recorded Eisteddfod (1176)
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Dinefwr prince celebrated throughout Brut y Tywysogion as chief statesman of southern Wales.

nodes.name: King Madog ap Maredudd & Owain Cyfeiliog of Powys
nodes.role: Last Sole King of Unified Powys & Poet-Prince
sources: W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Holders of Mathrafal whose partition of Powys shaped Brut y Tywysogion and Hirlas Owain.

nodes.name: King Bridei I (Brude mac Maelchon) of the Picts
nodes.role: High King of Fortriu / Pictland & Contemporary of St. Columba
sources: W.F. Skene, Chronicles of the Picts and Scots
Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
nodes.notes: Recorded by Bede and Skene's Pictish Chronicles receiving St. Columba at Inverness and halting Dal Riata expansion.

nodes.name: King Oengus I mac Fergusa (Onuist) of the Picts
nodes.role: Great Overlord of Pictland & Subduer of Dal Riata
sources: W.F. Skene, Chronicles of the Picts and Scots
nodes.notes: Unified northern Scotland in the Annals of Ulster and Skene's Pictish Chronicles.

nodes.name: King Causantin II (Constantine mac Aeda) of Alba
nodes.role: King of Alba (Scotland) & Allied Sovereign at Brunanburh
sources: W.F. Skene, Chronicles of the Picts and Scots
nodes.notes: Grandson of Kenneth MacAlpin who forged the Kingdom of Alba across 43 regnal years.

nodes.name: King Aethelberht of Kent & Queen Bertha
nodes.role: Bretwalda, First Christian Anglo-Saxon King & Merovingian Princess
sources: Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
nodes.notes: Married Frankish Princess Bertha; welcomed Augustine of Canterbury (597 CE) in Bede Book I & Sammes.

nodes.name: King Raedwald of East Anglia (Wuffingas Bretwalda)
nodes.role: King of East Anglia & Champion of Edwin of Northumbria
sources: Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
nodes.notes: Installed Edwin on the Northumbrian throne at the River Idle; widely linked with Sutton Hoo Ship Burial.

nodes.name: King Penda of Mercia (Pagan Warrior Bretwalda)
nodes.role: Iclingas King of Mercia
sources: Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
nodes.notes: Allied with Cadwallon ap Cadfan of Gwynedd in Bede Book II-III before falling at Winwaed.

nodes.name: King Oswiu of Northumbria & Abbess St. Hilda of Whitby
nodes.role: Northumbrian Bretwalda & Convener of Synod of Whitby (664 CE)
sources: Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
nodes.notes: Presided over the Synod of Whitby reconciling Celtic and Roman Easter traditions in Bede Book III-IV.

nodes.name: Kings Wulfhere, Aethelred & Aethelbald of Mercia
nodes.role: Christian Mercian Supremacy Sovereigns
sources: Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
nodes.notes: Sons and successors of Penda uniting Middle England ahead of Offa's overlordship.

nodes.name: Aethelflaed, Lady of the Mercians
nodes.role: Eldest Child of Alfred the Great & Sovereign Ruler of Mercia
sources: Venerable Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation (1723)
Aylett Sammes, Antiquities of Ancient Britain
W.F. Skene, The Four Ancient Books of Wales Vol. 1
Brut y Tywysogion (Chronicle of the Princes)
nodes.notes: Allied with Edward the Elder to fortify Mercian burhs and conquer the Five Boroughs from the Danelaw.

nodes.name: Duke Huan of Qi (Jiang Xiaobai, r. 685 - 643 BCE)
nodes.role: First of the Five Hegemons of the Spring & Autumn Period
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Jiang Ziya; convened the Nine Assemblies of Feudal Lords defending the Zhou Son of Heaven (Shiji Ch. 32).

nodes.name: Guan Zhong (Premier of Qi & Statesman)
nodes.role: Prime Minister to Duke Huan of Qi & Fiscal Reformer
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Architect of salt-and-iron monopolies and hegemonic confederation praised by Confucius in Shiji & Analects.

nodes.name: Duke Wen of Jin (Chong'er, r. 636 - 628 BCE)
nodes.role: Second Hegemon of Spring & Autumn China; Victor at Chengpu
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Spent nineteen years in exile across Di, Qi, Song, Chu, and Qin before victorious return in Shiji Ch. 39.

nodes.name: Duke Mu of Qin (Ying Renhao, r. 659 - 621 BCE)
nodes.role: Hegemon of the Western Rong & Father-in-Law of Jin Princes
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Sheltered and restored Duke Wen of Jin while expanding Qin across twelve Rong states (Shiji Ch. 5).

nodes.name: Duke Xiang of Song (Zi Zifu, r. 650 - 637 BCE)
nodes.role: Shang-Descended Duke & Chivalrous Spring & Autumn Hegemon
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Upheld Shang ancestral rites at Mengzhu and fought King Cheng of Chu at the Hong River (Shiji Ch. 38).

nodes.name: King Zhuang of Chu (Mi Lu, r. 613 - 591 BCE)
nodes.role: Southern Hegemon of Chu Who Asked the Weight of Zhou's Cauldrons
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Reformed Chu administration with Sunshu Ao and triumphed at Bi (Shiji Ch. 40).

nodes.name: King Helu of Wu (Ji Guang, r. 514 - 496 BCE)
nodes.role: Zhou-Descended King of Wu & Patron of Sun Tzu
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Built Suzhou (Gusu) and captured Ying, capital of Chu, aided by Wu Zixu and Sun Wu (Shiji Ch. 31).

nodes.name: Wu Zixu (Wu Yun, Chu Nobleman & Strategist of Wu)
nodes.role: Grand Tutor of Wu & Rival of Bo Pi
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Escaped Chu vendetta to counsel Kings Helu and Fuchai of Wu in Shiji Ch. 66.

nodes.name: King Fuchai of Wu (r. 495 - 473 BCE)
nodes.role: Final King of Wu & Victor at Fuqiao / Presider at Huangchi
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Defeated Goujian at Fuqiao and presided over the Huangchi summit before Yue's counter-conquest (Shiji Ch. 31).

nodes.name: King Goujian of Yue (Si Goujian, r. 496 - 465 BCE)
nodes.role: Xia-Descended King of Yue & Final Hegemon
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Shao Kang of Xia; endured captivity in Wu ('sleeping on brushwood, tasting gall') to annex Wu in 473 BCE (Shiji Ch. 41).

nodes.name: Fan Li & Beauty Xi Shi of Yue
nodes.role: Strategist of Yue & Ancestor of Merchant Patronage
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Masterminded Yue's twenty-year revival under Goujian before retiring across Lake Tai as 'Lord Tao Zhu' (Shiji Ch. 41).

nodes.name: Marquis Wen of Wei (Wei Si, r. 445 - 396 BCE)
nodes.role: Founder of Partition-of-Jin Hegemony & Patron of Zixia
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Initiated Legalist-Confucian reforms with Li Kui, Wu Qi, and Ximen Bao (Shiji Ch. 44).

nodes.name: Duke Xiao of Qin & Lord Shang Yang (Wei Yang)
nodes.role: Sovereign & Architect of Qin's Legalist Ascendancy
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Codified agrarian-military ranks across Qin (359 BCE), laying the direct foundation for Qin Shi Huang (Shiji Ch. 5 & 68).

nodes.name: King Wuling of Zhao (Zhao Yong, r. 325 - 299 BCE)
nodes.role: Champion of Mounted Cavalry Reform (Hu Fu Qi She)
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Adopted nomadic horse-archery across Zhao's northern frontier against the Linhu and Loufan (Shiji Ch. 43).

nodes.name: Qu Yuan of Chu (Royal Mi Statesman & Poet)
nodes.role: Junior Chu Royal Line Poet of the Chu Ci
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Grandson-collateral of King Wu of Chu; authored Li Sao and mourned Ying's fall in Shiji Ch. 84.

nodes.name: The Four Lords of the Warring States (Mengchang, Pingyuan, Xinling & Chunshen)
nodes.role: Princely Patrons of Qi, Zhao, Wei & Chu
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Tian Wen, Zhao Sheng, Wei Wuji, and Huang Xie profiled across Shiji Ch. 75-78 for maintaining anti-Qin coalitions.

nodes.name: Chancellor Lu Buwei & Grand Councilor Li Si of Qin
nodes.role: Architects of Qin Shi Huang's Unification
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Supervised the Lvshi Chunqiu encyclopedia, script standardization, and commanderies of the First Empire (Shiji Ch. 85 & 87).

nodes.name: Master Yan Ying of Qi & Mencius (Meng Ke)
nodes.role: Qi Statesman & Second Sage of Confucianism
sources: Edouard Chavannes, Les Memoires Historiques de Se-ma Ts'ien (Shiji Vol. 5)
nodes.notes: Yan Ying stabilized Qi's statecraft; Mencius (studied under Zisi) defended benevolent kingship across Qi and Wei.

nodes.name: King Samaratungga & Princess Pramodhawardhani (Sailendra)
nodes.role: Sailendra Monarchs of Java & Completers of Borobudur
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: United Sailendra Buddhist builders of Borobudur with Sanjaya Mataram via marriage to Rakai Pikatan (Stokvis).

nodes.name: King Airlangga of Kahuripan (East Java)
nodes.role: Balinese-Javanese Restorer of Medang (r. 1019 - 1045 CE)
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Son of Udayana of Bali; partitioned his kingdom into Janggala and Kediri for his sons.

nodes.name: Kings Ken Arok & Kertanegara of Singhasari
nodes.role: Founder & Final Sovereign of Singhasari; Ancestor of Majapahit
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Kertanegara projected Pamalayu power across Sumatra and defied Kublai Khan ahead of Raden Wijaya.

nodes.name: Sultan Iskandar Muda of Aceh Darussalam
nodes.role: Golden-Age Sultan of Aceh (r. 1607 - 1636 CE)
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Extended Acehnese maritime sovereignty across Sumatra and Pahang while exchanging envoys with Ottomans and Europe.

nodes.name: Sultan Agung Adi Prabu Hanyakrakusuma of Mataram
nodes.role: Great Susuhunan / Sultan of Islamic Mataram (Java)
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Grandson of Panembahan Senapati; unified central and eastern Java and struck the Dutch at Batavia (1628-1629).

nodes.name: Kings Bhadravarman, Indravarman II & Che Bong Nga of Champa
nodes.role: Sovereigns of Cham Kingdoms (My Son / Vijaya)
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Maintained Sanskrit-Austronesian Cham civilization along central Vietnam between Dai Viet and Angkor.

nodes.name: Sultan Shari'ful Hashem & Paduka Batara of Sulu
nodes.role: Sultans of Sulu & Eastern Maritime Envoy to Yongle
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Documented in Ming annals and Sulu tarsila genealogies linking Brunei, Sulu, and Malacca maritime houses.

nodes.name: King Sho Hashi of Ryukyu (Unifier of Three Kingdoms, 1429 CE)
nodes.role: Founder of the Unified Kingdom of Ryukyu (Okinawa)
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: United Hokuzan, Chuzan, and Nanzan at Shuri Castle, opening Ryukyu's maritime trade across East and SE Asia.

nodes.name: Kings Sho Shin & Final King Sho Tai of Ryukyu
nodes.role: Second Sho Dynasty Sovereigns of Shuri Castle
sources: A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Sho Shin centralized Ryukyuan nobility; Sho Tai remained king until the 1879 Meiji transition.

nodes.name: Emperor Mihira Bhoja I of Gurjara-Pratihara
nodes.role: Overlord of Kannauj & Tripartite Imperial Rival
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
A.M.H.J. Stokvis, Manuel d'Histoire, de Genealogie et de Chronologie
nodes.notes: Extended Pratihara rule from Punjab to Bihar and Narmada, praised by Arab travelers for cavalry strength (Duff).

nodes.name: Kings Gopala I & Dharmapala of Pala Bengal
nodes.role: Founders of the Pala Empire & Patrons of Vikramashila
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Gopala ended Matsyanyaya anarchy in Bengal; Dharmapala presided over the imperial assembly at Kannauj (Duff).

nodes.name: Kings Devapala & Mahipala I of Pala Bengal
nodes.role: Pala Emperors & Restorers of Gauda
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Devapala received envoys from Balaputradeva of Srivijaya for Nalanda endowment; Mahipala revived Pala power.

nodes.name: Raja Bhoja Paramara of Dhar (Malwa)
nodes.role: Paramara Emperor, Polymath & Patron of Bhojpur
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Authored Samaranganasutradhara, founded Bhojeshwar and Bhoj Shala, and ruled central India (Duff & Tod).

nodes.name: Kings Dhanga & Vidyadhara Chandela of Jejakabhukti
nodes.role: Rajput Builders of Khajuraho Temples
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Defended Kalinjar and central India during early eleventh-century Ghaznavid campaigns (Duff).

nodes.name: Siddharaja Jayasimha & Kumarapala Chaulukya (Solanki)
nodes.role: Solanki Kings of Anhilwara Patan (Gujarat)
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Presided over Gujarat's golden literary and architectural age alongside Acharya Hemachandra.

nodes.name: Emperor Vikramaditya VI of Western Chalukya (Kalyani)
nodes.role: Institutor of the Chalukya-Vikrama Era & Patron of Bilhana
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Longest-reigning Western Chalukya emperor, governing from Kalyani across Maharashtra and Karnataka.

nodes.name: Ganapatideva & Queen Rudrama Devi of Kakatiya Warangal
nodes.role: Kakatiya Emperor & Sovereign Ruling Queen of Andhra
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Queen Rudrama Devi governed Warangal for thirty years, earning the praise of Marco Polo in South India (Duff).

nodes.name: Bappa Rawal, Maharana Kumbha & Maharana Sanga of Mewar
nodes.role: Sisodia Guhila Maharanas of Chittor & Kumbhalgarh
sources: C. Mabel Duff (Rickmers), Chronology of India
James Tod, Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Anchored by James Tod Vol. 1 as Solar-lineage guardians of Mewar bridging Guhila antiquity to Maharana Pratap.

nodes.name: Hjorleifr Hrodmarsson (Foster-Brother of Ingolfur)
nodes.role: Co-Settler of Iceland & Husband of Helga Arnardottir
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Sworn blood-brother of Ingolfur Arnarson; landed at Hjorleifshofdi (Landnamabok Part I).

nodes.name: Bjorn the Easterner & Helgi Bjolan Ketilsson
nodes.role: Hebridean Sons of Ketil Flatnose & Settlers of Breidafjord
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Brothers of Aud the Deep-Minded who colonized Kjalarnes and Borgarholt (Landnamabok Part I-II).

nodes.name: Olaf Feilan & Thord Gellir (Hvamm Founders)
nodes.role: Grandson & Great-Grandson of Aud the Deep-Minded
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Established Iceland's Quarter Courts (Fjordungathing) in Laxdaela & Landnamabok Part II.

nodes.name: Skalla-Grim Kveldulfsson of Borg
nodes.role: Early Settler of Borgarfjordur & Ancestor of the Myramenn
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Fled Harald Fairhair's Norway after Thorolf's fall; settled Borg (Landnamabok Part II).

nodes.name: Egill Skallagrimsson of Borg (Skald & Chieftain)
nodes.role: Warrior-Poet of Egils Saga & Son of Skalla-Grim
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Served King Athelstan at Brunanburh and composed Sonatorrek; forebear of both Ari Frodi and Snorri Sturluson.

nodes.name: Hrollaugr Rognvaldsson (Half-Brother of Rollo of Normandy)
nodes.role: Son of Jarl Rognvald of More & Settler of Sida
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Crossed from Orkney/Norway to eastern Iceland; his grandson Sidu-Hallr championed Iceland's conversion (Landnamabok IV).

nodes.name: Snorri Godi (Thorgrimsson of Helgafell)
nodes.role: Priesthood-Chieftain of Snaefellsnes & Christian Diplomat
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Key statesman in Eyrbyggja, Njals, and Laxdaela sagas; secured the peaceful 1000 CE Althing vote.

nodes.name: Thorgeir Ljosvetningagodi (Lawspeaker at Althing 1000 CE)
nodes.role: Althing Lawspeaker Who Proclaimed Iceland's Peaceful Conversion
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Delivered the unifying 999/1000 CE Althing compromise preserving private heritage under public Christian law.

nodes.name: Njall Thorgeirsson of Bergthorshvoll & Gunnar of Hlidarendi
nodes.role: Jurist & Chieftain Heroes of Southern Iceland
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Central families of southern Rangavellir documented in Landnamabok Part V and Brennu-Njals Saga.

nodes.name: Thorfinn Karlsefni & Snorri Thorfinnsson (Born in Vinland)
nodes.role: Husband of Gudrid Thorbjarnardottir & First European Child Born in North America
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Settled Skagafjordur after leading the Vinland expedition; ancestral to three early Icelandic bishops.

nodes.name: Ari Thorgilsson ('Ari the Learned', Author of Islendingabok)
nodes.role: Father of Icelandic Vernacular Historiography
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Descended from Olaf Feilan and Aud the Deep-Minded; compiled the foundational history of Iceland and Greenland.

nodes.name: Bishops Isleifr Gizurarson & Gizurr Isleifsson of Skalholt
nodes.role: First Native Bishops of Iceland (Skalholt)
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Haukdaelir chieftain-bishops related to Sidu-Hallr and Gudrid's clerical lineage.

nodes.name: Saemundr Sigfusson ('the Learned' of Oddi)
nodes.role: Scholar of Oddi, Paris-Educated Historian & Foster-House of Snorri Sturluson
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Jon Loftsson of Oddi who educated Snorri Sturluson.

nodes.name: Hvamm-Sturla & Snorri Sturluson (Author of Prose Edda & Heimskringla)
nodes.role: Lawspeaker of Iceland & Great Chronicler of Norse Kings
sources: Thomas Ellwood, The Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, 1898)
nodes.notes: Descended from Egill Skallagrimsson and Olaf Feilan; authored the Prose Edda and Heimskringla.

nodes.name: High Priest Uzzi ben Bukki of Mount Gerizim
nodes.role: Samaritan High Priest Preserving the Hidden Tabernacle
sources: Moses Gaster, The Samaritans: Their History, Doctrines and Literature
Samaritan Chronicle of Joshua
nodes.notes: Samaritan Chronicles of Joshua & Shalshalat ha-Kohanim record Uzzi concealing the Tabernacle vessels on Mount Gerizim.

nodes.name: Baba Rabba (Great Father & Reformer of Samaria, 4th c. CE)
nodes.role: Samaritan High Priestly Statesman & Synagogue Founder
sources: Moses Gaster, The Samaritans: Their History, Doctrines and Literature
Samaritan Chronicle of Joshua
nodes.notes: Eldest son of High Priest Nathanael; divided Samaria into twelve administrative regions and revived liturgical learning (Gaster).

nodes.name: Tebah Marqah & Amram Dare (Samaritan Liturgists)
nodes.role: Father-Son Founders of Samaritan Aramaic Literature (Memar Marqah)
sources: Moses Gaster, The Samaritans: Their History, Doctrines and Literature
Samaritan Chronicle of Joshua
nodes.notes: Flourished under Baba Rabba; composed foundational Aramaic hymns and Memar Marqah (Gaster).

nodes.name: King Shobach of Armenia & Nabih of Gilead
nodes.role: Adversaries & Coalition Rulers in Samaritan Book of Joshua
sources: Moses Gaster, The Samaritans: Their History, Doctrines and Literature
Samaritan Chronicle of Joshua
nodes.notes: Unique Arabic-Samaritan Joshua romance narrating Joshua's deliverance by Nabih, prince of Reuben/Gilead.

nodes.name: Bitenosh, Lamech & 1QapGen Geographic Earth Partition
nodes.role: Aramaic Dead Sea Apocryphon Narrative of Noah & Abraham
sources: Dead Sea Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
R.H. Charles, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
Louis Ginzberg, Legends of the Jews
nodes.notes: Genesis Apocryphon (Cols. II-XXI) preserves Lamech-Bitenosh dialogue, Noah's world survey, and Abraham's Jordan/Nile circuit.

nodes.name: Melcha (Wife of Levi) & Priestly Ascension
nodes.role: Patriarchal Wife & Kohath-Amram Levitical Stem
sources: Dead Sea Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
R.H. Charles, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
Louis Ginzberg, Legends of the Jews
nodes.notes: Testament of Levi 11-12 names Melcha (daughter of Bethuel/Aram) and gives exact dates for Kohath and Amram.

nodes.name: Shua, Tamar & Achor-Hazor Royal Wars of Judah
nodes.role: Testament of Judah Genealogical & Military Tradition
sources: Dead Sea Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
R.H. Charles, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
Louis Ginzberg, Legends of the Jews
nodes.notes: R.H. Charles's Testament of Judah supplements Genesis 38 with heroic wars against Canaanite kings of Hazor and Tapuah.

nodes.name: Rotheus (Chaldean Grandfather of Bilhah) & Zilpah
nodes.role: Paternal Pedigree of Bilhah & Naphtali
sources: Dead Sea Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
R.H. Charles, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
Louis Ginzberg, Legends of the Jews
nodes.notes: Testament of Naphtali 1 identifies Rotheus, captured brother-in-law of Laban, as Bilhah's father.

nodes.name: Elders of Reuben & Simeon (Massekhet Shevatim)
nodes.role: Moral Warnings & Tribal Matriarchs in Testaments
sources: Dead Sea Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
R.H. Charles, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
Louis Ginzberg, Legends of the Jews
nodes.notes: Testaments of Reuben and Simeon preserve tribal demographic traditions and Egyptian sojourning notes.

nodes.name: Serah bat Asher (Long-Lived Keeper of Joseph's Tomb)
nodes.role: Asherite Daughter & Memory-Bearer in Legends of the Jews
sources: Dead Sea Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
R.H. Charles, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
Louis Ginzberg, Legends of the Jews
nodes.notes: Louis Ginzberg compiles Midrashic tradition of Serah surviving from Jacob's descent to Egypt to David's reign.

nodes.name: Shaykhs of the Kababish Nurab (Fadl Allah & Ali al-Tom)
nodes.role: Paramount Camel-Nomad Arab Confederation of Northern Kordofan
sources: H.A. MacMichael, The Tribes of Northern and Central Kordofan
nodes.notes: MacMichael documents Kababish Juhayna/Quraish oral nisbas centering on Bayoda and northern Kordofan.

nodes.name: Dar Hamid & Jawama'a Arab Tribes of Kordofan
nodes.role: Juhayna & Ja'aliyin Pastoralist Houses around Bara
sources: H.A. MacMichael, The Tribes of Northern and Central Kordofan
nodes.notes: Mapped in MacMichael's Kordofan pedigrees linking Dar Hamid, Ferahna, and Awlad Akoi.

nodes.name: Baggara Hawazma & Messiria Confederations (Kordofan)
nodes.role: Atiyah / Juhayna Cattle-Herding Confederations of Southern Kordofan
sources: H.A. MacMichael, The Tribes of Northern and Central Kordofan
nodes.notes: MacMichael details Hawazma and Messiria migrations along Bahr al-Arab and the Nuba foothills.

nodes.name: Pharaoh Ramesses III (Medinet Habu, Recorded by Norden 1737)
nodes.role: Final Great New Kingdom Warrior-Pharaoh
sources: Frederik Ludvig Norden, Antiquities of Egypt, Nubia and Thebes
nodes.notes: F.L. Norden's pioneering 1737-1757 illustrated Nile expedition first published Medinet Habu, Thebes, and Dendera to Europe.

nodes.name: Colossi of Amenhotep III & Ramesseum Monumental Line (Norden)
nodes.role: Theban Monumental Dynastic Horizon Documented by Norden
sources: Frederik Ludvig Norden, Antiquities of Egypt, Nubia and Thebes
nodes.notes: Norden mapped Luxor, Karnak, and the Colossi of Memnon twenty years before the Napoleonic Description.

nodes.name: Cataract Temple Builders of Philae, Kalabsha & Derr (Norden)
nodes.era: Late New Kingdom to Meroitic Era
nodes.role: Nubian-Egyptian Temple Corridors Surveyed by Norden (1737)
sources: Frederik Ludvig Norden, Antiquities of Egypt, Nubia and Thebes
nodes.notes: Norden was the first modern European explorer to chart Lower Nubia down to Derr above Philae.

nodes.name: King Turnus of the Rutuli (Ardea)
nodes.role: King of Ardea & Rival of Aeneas for Lavinia
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Allied with Amata of Laurentum and Mezentius before falling in single combat against Aeneas.

nodes.name: King Mezentius & Lausus of Caere (Etruria)
nodes.role: Etruscan King of Agylla / Caere
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Detailed in Dionysius of Halicarnassus Book I negotiating treaty with Ascanius and Turnus.

nodes.name: King Titus Tatius of the Sabines (Co-Ruler with Romulus)
nodes.role: Sabine Co-King of Rome at Quirinal Hill
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Forged the Romano-Sabine dual monarchy alongside Romulus following the Sabine intervention.

nodes.name: Publius Valerius Publicola (Consul 509 BCE)
nodes.role: Co-Founder of the Roman Republic & Colleague of Brutus
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Replaced Collatinus alongside Lucius Junius Brutus; carried Provocatio citizen-appeal laws (Kennett).

nodes.name: Horatius Cocles, Mucius Scaevola & Cloelia
nodes.role: Defenders of Early Republican Rome Against Lars Porsenna
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Exemplars of Pons Sublicius defence celebrated across Kennett's Roman Antiquities and Livy.

nodes.name: Gaius Marcius Coriolanus (+ Mother Veturia)
nodes.role: Conqueror of Corioli & Volscian Exile
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Dionysius Book VII-VIII and Kennett highlight Veturia and Volumnia sparing Rome from the Volscian march.

nodes.name: Marcus Furius Camillus ('Second Founder of Rome')
nodes.role: Five-Time Dictator & Liberator After Gallic Sack (390 BCE)
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Conquered Veii and reorganized post-Allia Roman citizen-legions (Kennett).

nodes.name: Censor Appius Claudius Caecus (Builder of Via Appia)
nodes.role: Patrician Censor, Jurist & Orator Against Pyrrhus
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Constructed the Aqua Appia and Via Appia (312 BCE) and rallied the Senate against Pyrrhus's peace.

nodes.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus ('Cunctator')
nodes.role: Dictator, Shield of Rome in the Second Punic War
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Engineered the Fabian attrition strategy saving Rome after Cannae alongside Marcellus and Scipio.

nodes.name: Marcus Claudius Marcellus ('Sword of Rome', Five-Time Consul)
nodes.role: Conqueror of Syracuse (212 BCE) & Winner of Spolia Opima
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Won Nola and captured Syracuse despite Archimedes's engines during the Second Punic War (Kennett).

nodes.name: Pliny the Younger (Gaius Plinius Caecilius Secundus)
nodes.role: Roman Senator, Governor of Bithynia & Panegyrist of Trajan
sources: Pliny the Younger, Panegyric on Trajan
nodes.notes: Delivered the consular Panegyricus to Emperor Trajan (100 CE) and preserved early imperial Bithynia correspondence.

nodes.name: St. Isidore of Seville (Etymologies Book IX: Nations & Tongues)
nodes.role: Archbishop of Seville & Systematic Table-of-Nations Synthesizer
sources: St. Isidore of Seville, Etymologies Book IX
James Ussher, The Annals of the World
John Blair, Chronology and History of the World (1753)
William Guthrie & John Gray, A General History of the World (1764)
George Rawlinson, Origin of Nations
Charles Foster Kent, Narratives of the Beginnings of Hebrew History (1904)
nodes.notes: Book IX of the Etymologies maps all Mediterranean, Germanic, Gothic, and Near Eastern peoples back to Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

nodes.name: Archbishop James Ussher (Annales Veteris Testamenti, 1650)
nodes.role: Primate of All Ireland & Architect of 4004 BCE Chronology
sources: St. Isidore of Seville, Etymologies Book IX
James Ussher, The Annals of the World
John Blair, Chronology and History of the World (1753)
William Guthrie & John Gray, A General History of the World (1764)
George Rawlinson, Origin of Nations
Charles Foster Kent, Narratives of the Beginnings of Hebrew History (1904)
nodes.notes: Synchronized Masoretic biblical reigns with Nabonassar, Julian Period, Olympiads, and Roman Fasti.

nodes.name: Rev. John Blair (Chronology & History of the World, 1753)
nodes.role: Author of Fifty-Six Comparative Universal Chronological Tables
sources: St. Isidore of Seville, Etymologies Book IX
James Ussher, The Annals of the World
John Blair, Chronology and History of the World (1753)
William Guthrie & John Gray, A General History of the World (1764)
George Rawlinson, Origin of Nations
Charles Foster Kent, Narratives of the Beginnings of Hebrew History (1904)
nodes.notes: Published the 1753 London folio harmonizing ancient Near Eastern, Greek, Roman, and European sovereigns.

nodes.name: William Guthrie & John Gray (13-Vol Universal History, 1764)
nodes.role: Scottish Historians of A General History of the World (1764)
sources: St. Isidore of Seville, Etymologies Book IX
James Ussher, The Annals of the World
John Blair, Chronology and History of the World (1753)
William Guthrie & John Gray, A General History of the World (1764)
George Rawlinson, Origin of Nations
Charles Foster Kent, Narratives of the Beginnings of Hebrew History (1904)
nodes.notes: Synthesized European, Islamic, Steppe, and East Asian dynastic histories from creation to the mid-18th century.

nodes.name: Canon George Rawlinson (The Origin of Nations, 1877)
nodes.role: Camden Professor of Ancient History & Ethnographer of Genesis 10
sources: St. Isidore of Seville, Etymologies Book IX
James Ussher, The Annals of the World
John Blair, Chronology and History of the World (1753)
William Guthrie & John Gray, A General History of the World (1764)
George Rawlinson, Origin of Nations
Charles Foster Kent, Narratives of the Beginnings of Hebrew History (1904)
nodes.notes: Compared Genesis 10 ethnology against newly deciphered Egyptian monuments and Assyrian cuneiform.

nodes.name: Charles Foster Kent (Narratives of the Beginnings, 1904)
nodes.role: Woolsey Professor at Yale & Comparative Ancient Source Historian
sources: St. Isidore of Seville, Etymologies Book IX
James Ussher, The Annals of the World
John Blair, Chronology and History of the World (1753)
William Guthrie & John Gray, A General History of the World (1764)
George Rawlinson, Origin of Nations
Charles Foster Kent, Narratives of the Beginnings of Hebrew History (1904)
nodes.notes: Analyzed J, E, P, and Babylonian Flood parallels across early Hebrew genealogical narratives.

nodes.name: Basil Kennett (Romae Antiquae Notitia, 1696/1793)
nodes.role: Principal of St. Edmund Hall & Classical Roman Antiquarian
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities
Basil Kennett, Romae Antiquae Notitia (1793)
nodes.notes: Codified Roman magistracies, priesthoods, gentes, and republican hero lineages for 18th-century scholarship.
